evidence.title: AI data centers: How much are ratepayers on the hook for?

occurrences.checkable_against: Utility power-purchase contracts, retail tariffs and regulatory decisions
occurrences.quote_span: How much of the increase is passed on to residential customers and when, depends on utilities' power-purchasing contracts, retail rates and regulatory decisions about who pays, according to Lucy Qiu, a professor at the School of Public Policy at the University of Maryland.
occurrences.speaker: Lucy Qiu
occurrences.subject: AI data center electricity costs

occurrences.checkable_against: Data-center utility contracts and non-disclosure agreements
occurrences.quote_span: Even so, "a single, clean number" that applies nationwide is just not possible, Harvard's Peskoe says, because "a lot of the data about how much particular data centers are paying is hidden behind non-disclosure agreements."
occurrences.speaker: Ari Peskoe
occurrences.subject: AI data center electricity costs

occurrences.checkable_against: Utility rate filings and customer electricity bills
occurrences.quote_span: "In many cases, it is just ultimately going to end up in customers' bills."

occurrences.subject: AI data center electricity costs

occurrences.checkable_against: Utility infrastructure accounting and cost-allocation records
occurrences.quote_span: "It really depends on the scale of the upgrade and also how utilities are doing the accounting of that different share, whether it's being used solely by the data centers or also being shared by other customers," Qiu says.
occurrences.speaker: Lucy Qiu
occurrences.subject: AI data center electricity costs

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. grid planning documents and electricity-demand forecasts

occurrences.checkable_against: Electric-grid resiliency and outage records near data centers
occurrences.quote_span: There's also evidence, Qui says, that resiliency — the ability to survive high-impact events such as extreme heat and to recover from outages — is better for people living near data centers due to the robust infrastructure those facilities require.
occurrences.speaker: Lucy Qiu
occurrences.subject: AI data center electricity costs

occurrences.checkable_against: Utility tariff schedules and customer-class electricity rates
occurrences.quote_span: Big customers like AI data centers pay less per kilowatt hour for power than residential customers do.
